cases.sentence: Старая седая ___, ходившая за ними следом, села осторожно против него и насторожила уши.
cases.translation: The old gray weasel, which had been following behind them, sat down carefully facing him and pricked up its ears.
cases.explain: «Ласка» is the grammatical subject of «села», so it stands in the Nominative case.

cases.translation: From beyond the river a cuckoo could be heard.
cases.explain: The preposition «из-за» (from behind/beyond) governs the Genitive case, hence «речки».

cases.sentence: Сам он вернулся на другой край, к двойняшке ___.
cases.translation: He himself went back to the other edge, to a twin birch tree.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (toward) governs the Dative case, hence «берёзе».

cases.sentence: Левин слез и провел Облонского на ___ мшистой и топкой полянки, уже освободившейся от снега.
cases.translation: Levin got down and led Oblonsky to the corner of the mossy, boggy clearing, already free of snow.
cases.explain: The preposition «на» expressing motion toward a place governs the Accusative here, hence «угол».

cases.sentence: Ястреб, неспешно махая крыльями, пролетел высоко над дальним ___.
cases.translation: A hawk, slowly flapping its wings, flew high over the distant forest.
cases.explain: The preposition «над» (above, over) governs the Instrumental case, hence «лесом».

cases.sentence: Место тяги было недалеко над речкой в мелком ___.
cases.translation: The woodcock-flight spot was not far, above a little river, in a sparse aspen grove.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» (in) denoting location governs the Prepositional case, hence «осиннике».

reading.ru: Место тяги было недалеко над речкой в мелком осиннике.
reading.question: Where was the spot for the woodcock flight (тяга)?
options: Not far, above a river, in a sparse aspen grove
At the edge of the village
reading.correct: Not far, above a river, in a sparse aspen grove
reading.explain: The text states the flight spot was near a river in a sparse aspen grove.

reading.ru: Старая седая ласка, ходившая за ними следом, села осторожно против него и насторожила уши.
reading.question: What animal had been following the two men and sat facing Levin?
reading.explain: The text describes an old gray weasel (ласка) that followed them and sat facing Levin.

reading.ru: Мелкие птицы щебетали и изредка пролетали с дерева на дерево.
reading.question: What were the small birds doing?
options: Chirping and occasionally flying from tree to tree
reading.correct: Chirping and occasionally flying from tree to tree
reading.explain: The small birds are described as chirping and flying occasionally between trees.

reading.ru: «Каково! Слышно и видно, как трава растет!»
reading.question: What did Levin remark to himself about the stillness of the forest?
options: That he could hear and see the grass growing
That it was too cold to hunt
That the birds had stopped singing
reading.correct: That he could hear and see the grass growing
reading.explain: Levin says to himself that one can hear and see the grass growing, marveling at the silence.

reading.ru: Ястреб, неспешно махая крыльями, пролетел высоко над дальним лесом.
reading.question: What bird flew slowly over the distant forest?
reading.explain: The text describes a hawk flying high over the distant forest, flapping its wings unhurriedly.

reading.question: What sound came from beyond the river?
reading.explain: A cuckoo could be heard calling from beyond the river.

reading.ru: «Каково! Уж кукушка!» — сказал Степан Аркадьевич, выходя из-за куста.
reading.question: Who exclaimed about the cuckoo, stepping out from behind a bush?
reading.explain: The text says Stepan Arkadyevich said this while stepping out from behind a bush.

reading.ru: «А это что кричит?» — спросил Облонский, обращая внимание Левина на протяжное гуканье, как будто тонким голоском шаля ржал жеребенок.
reading.question: What did Oblonsky ask Levin about?
options: A strange drawn-out cry he heard
reading.correct: A strange drawn-out cry he heard
reading.explain: Oblonsky asked what was making the drawn-out cry that sounded like a foal neighing thinly.

reading.question: What did Levin say was making the sound Oblonsky asked about?
reading.explain: Levin explains that the sound is made by a male hare (заяц-самец).

reading.ru: И, трепля крыльями, как бы стараясь удержаться на воздухе, птица остановилась, постояла мгновение и тяжело шлепнулась о топкую землю.
reading.question: What happened to the bird after it was shot?
options: It fluttered, paused, and fell heavily to the boggy ground
It landed safely in a tree
reading.correct: It fluttered, paused, and fell heavily to the boggy ground
reading.explain: The bird fluttered its wings trying to stay airborne, then paused and fell heavily to the ground.

reading.ru: «Скверный промах из правого ствола», — отвечал Степан Аркадьевич, заряжая ружье.
reading.question: What did Stepan Arkadyevich say about his shot?
options: It was a bad miss from the right barrel
He had run out of ammunition
reading.correct: It was a bad miss from the right barrel
reading.explain: Stepan Arkadyevich calls his shot a bad miss from the right barrel while reloading his gun.

reading.ru: — Стива, — вдруг неожиданно сказал Левин, — что ж ты мне не скажешь, вышла твоя свояченица замуж или когда выходит?
reading.question: What did Levin suddenly ask Stepan Arkadyevich about?
options: Whether his sister-in-law had married or was about to
reading.correct: Whether his sister-in-law had married or was about to
reading.explain: Levin abruptly asks whether Stiva's sister-in-law (Kitty) has married or when she is marrying.

reading.ru: «Вот отлично! Общий!» — вскрикнул Левин и побежал с лаской в чащу отыскивать Вальшнепа.
reading.question: What did Levin do after they both shot at the same woodcock?
options: He ran with Laska into the thicket to find the woodcock
He gave up looking for it
He argued with Stepan Arkadyevich about who hit it
He reloaded his gun and left
reading.correct: He ran with Laska into the thicket to find the woodcock
reading.explain: Levin shouted with delight and ran with Laska into the thicket to retrieve the fallen woodcock.
